name: Restaurant Brands International Inc.
moat_justification: Durable, scaled restaurant brands on an asset-light royalty model with proven through-cycle cash generation, but the brands are mostly #2 in their categories, Tim Hortons is concentrated in a slow Canadian market, Popeyes US has declined in seven of the last eight quarters, and the equity sits behind heavy leverage — a step below a wide-moat franchisor.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 8.9x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Quality franchisor, moat 6/10, but priced for far more than its OE delivers — weighted IRR 9.2%, IV@15% $36.22 vs $71.06 price; clears 15% only near $36, and with a margin of safety in the high-$20s to mid-$30s.
moat_for: Four scaled brands, >33,000 restaurants, >95% franchised — royalties on system sales
Tim Hortons' entrenched Canada position (~41% of operating income)
International segment compounding — system-wide sales +10.7% in Q2 2026
Burger King US turnaround proving out — comparable sales +8.5% in Q2 2026
OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, including the 2020 COVID year
moat_against: No clear #1 brand position in the US — trails McDonald's / Chick-fil-A scale
Popeyes US comparable sales −5.1% in Q2 2026, negative in 7 of last 8 quarters
Tim Hortons Canada comparable sales only +0.1% in Q2 2026; beef/commodity cost pressure
Franchisee economics constrain royalties — units must earn enough to remodel and grow
High financial leverage — net debt $13.282B leaves a thin equity claim
